films.title: Foundation
films.description: Wethepeople's 2017 street-BMX full-length Foundation follows a year of filming across more than 10 countries and 20 cities. Filmed and edited by Cal Earnshaw, the 35-minute team film features full sections from Ed Zunda, Dillon Lloyd, Mike Curley, Pete Sawyer, Max Gaertig, Felix Prangenberg, Moritz Nussbaumer, Dan Kruk, and Jordan Godwin.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Public, embeddable complete DVD on Wethepeople BMX's official channel; exact runtime 35:31. The description identifies the project as the brand's third full-length, names the principal riders, credits filmmaker Cal Earnshaw, and confirms filming across more than 10 countries and 20 cities.
Contemporary March 2017 review confirms the original release year, full-length street-film format, 35-minute runtime, nine principal sections, and Cal Earnshaw's filming and editing credit.

DIG BMX's production feature confirms Wethepeople as producer, Cal Earnshaw as filmer, the 2016 production period, and trips through Italy, France, Great Britain, Germany, Latvia, Greece, Spain, and California before the early-2017 premiere.

films.title: It's Later Than You Think
films.description: Cult Crew's 2018 full-length It's Later Than You Think is the brand's third major team video. Filmed and edited by Veesh, the 38-minute DVD features Dakota Roche, Chase Hawk, Chase DeHart, Andrew Castaneda, Sean Ricany, Alex Kennedy, Corey Walsh, Dan Foley, and other members of the international Cult crew.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Public, embeddable complete DVD on Cult Crew's official channel; exact runtime 37:41. The upload is explicitly presented as the full DVD.
DIG BMX confirms the authorized complete-film upload, Cult Crew production, Veesh video credit, 2018 full-length release, and the film's section-by-section rider rollout.
Independent BMX filmography confirms the 2018 USA DVD release and Veesh editing credit.

BMX retailer metadata identifies the title as Cult Crew's third full-length, credits Veesh for filming and production, names principal riders, and describes approximately 40 minutes of worldwide street footage.
